question: Which three statements about Azure Databricks are true? (Choose three.)

options.text: It is an Azure-integrated analytics platform built on Apache Spark
Its notebooks let users combine multiple languages, such as Python, SQL, Scala, and R, in one workspace
It supports Delta Lake, which adds ACID transaction guarantees to data stored in a data lake
It is a fully managed relational database service for online transaction processing
It can read data only from storage located in the same Databricks workspace

explanation:
Azure Databricks is the first-party **Apache Spark-based analytics platform** on Azure, aimed at data engineering, data science, and machine learning at scale:

- **Built on Apache Spark** — Databricks provisions and manages Spark clusters, so teams get distributed compute without operating the infrastructure themselves.
- **Multi-language notebooks** — Collaborative notebooks support **Python, SQL, Scala, and R**, letting engineers and data scientists work together in a single environment (even mixing languages between cells).
- **Delta Lake** — An open-source storage layer that brings **ACID transactions**, schema enforcement, and time travel to files in a data lake — the foundation of the common medallion (bronze/silver/gold) lakehouse pattern.

**Why not the other options:**
- **A fully managed relational database service for OLTP** — Databricks is an **analytics** platform, not a transactional database. OLTP workloads on Azure belong to services such as Azure SQL Database.
- **It can read data only from storage in the same workspace** — Databricks routinely connects to **external storage**, most commonly Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 and Blob Storage, as well as many other sources. Data does not have to live "inside" the workspace.
category: Describe an Analytics Workload on Azure
